scope: What the panel's false-positive count actually consists of
correction_of_my_own_reading: I have been quoting fp_exhaustive_only = 176 as though it were per-frame false alarms. It is an event-level count, and the object-level picture is different: over 1460 frame-rows there are 31,700 objects not matching a label, of which 27,588 are ADJACENT - outside the corridor and correctly not hazards (16,507 of them labelled by the object-chain filter, working as designed). Counting only the hazard classes leaves 211 objects, about 0.14 per frame.

the_211_hazard_class_objects.distance: median 20 m, p10 8 m, p90 300 m

what_the_143_are: they concentrate on one case: an inserted 0.3 m box at 10.2 m, reported with 11-13 voxels and confirmed, on every frame of that case. The object IS reported; its box simply does not overlap the label at IoU >= 0.1, because the label is the visible support of a 0.3 m box (three or four returns) and the predicted box differs by more than the object is wide.
reading: the panel's false positives are dominated by box-convention mismatch on very small supports, the same limitation already recorded for this panel, not by spurious alarms on empty scenes - those are zero. So there is no precision defect to fix here; the honest number for the case is the empty-scene alarm rate, which is 0.0, and the far-field candidates that carry their own uncertainty.
why_it_matters: a scorer reading fp_exhaustive_only as a per-frame false-alarm rate would be wrong by two orders of magnitude, and I was one step away from reporting it that way myself
